title: Deploy succeeded, version never went live
scenario: "The pipeline says the deploy succeeded but users still see the old version. Argo CD is yellow." — Support ticket (game day GD-03)
mission: Ship a deploy PR with an image tag that does not exist, diagnose the ImagePullBackOff, and recover through Git.

steps.title: Inject (yourself)
steps.detail: PR that sets image.api.tag in gitops/envs/dev/values.yaml to v9.9.9; merge it.

steps.title: Observe
steps.detail: Why is the site still up?
steps.command: kubectl -n portal-dev get pods; kubectl -n portal-dev describe pod <new-pod>

steps.title: Recover
steps.detail: Revert the deploy PR — never edit the Deployment.

steps.title: Prevent
steps.detail: How does the app pipeline guarantee it only writes tags it just pushed?

criteria.text: All portal-dev deployments are Available with every pod Ready
Every image tag referenced by dev values exists in ACR
A revert commit of the bad tag exists on main

expectedResult: Old pods kept serving during the incident; Git history tells the story.

concepts.title: Rolling updates keep the old version alive
concepts.body: A Deployment update creates a new ReplicaSet and only removes old pods when new ones are Ready. If the new pods cannot start, the old ones keep serving: the site stays up, but the new version never goes live.

concepts.title: ImagePullBackOff
concepts.body: The kubelet cannot pull the image (wrong tag, missing registry permission, network). It retries with growing delays. `kubectl describe pod` shows the exact reason in Events, e.g. `manifest unknown` for a tag that does not exist.

concepts.title: Recovering through Git
concepts.body: With GitOps, the fix for a bad deploy PR is `git revert` of that PR (a new commit that undoes it). Argo CD then syncs the previous tag. Editing the Deployment by hand would be reverted by self-heal anyway.

example.title: reverting a merged PR
example.body: Find the merge commit, revert it on a branch and open a PR. For a squash merge there is a single parent, so no `-m` is needed:
example.code:
git log --oneline -5
git switch -c revert/bad-tag
git revert <sha>
git push -u origin revert/bad-tag
gh pr create --fill

glossary.def: Keeps N identical pods running; one per Deployment version.
Argo CD health states while a rollout is stuck.
New commit that undoes a previous one — history is preserved.

recovery: If the revert does not sync, check the Argo CD app is on auto-sync and the PR was merged to main.
dont: Do not delete the failing pods to "retry"
hints: A rolling update keeps old pods until new ones are Ready.
Events show manifest unknown for a missing tag.
git revert <merge-sha> on a branch, PR, merge.

interview.question: A deploy is green in CI but the new version never goes live. How do you investigate?
followUps: Why did users not notice an outage?

debrief: maxUnavailable/maxSurge kept the old ReplicaSet serving while the new one could not pull. The fix is a Git revert; the prevention is CI writing only tags it has just pushed (and, better, digests).

checker.plan: Read-only: kubectl get deploy/pods -o json, az acr repository show-tags, git log --grep Revert on main.

validation.notes: Checker not implemented yet; needs a running cluster.
